mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, the S&P 500 forward 60-day return tends to be positive due to expectations of prolonged accommodative policy and reduced risk aversion.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength and impending recession, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while INDPRO decreases by >2% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market weakening with supply shock
failure_condition: In 80% of similar trigger events, the SPX 20-day forward return is non-negative (median p-value > 0.5 in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in home sales (HOUST) of more than 5% for three consecutive months predicts stronger consumer confidence and supports a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: The 5-day SPX forward return is negative in all instances where the trigger occurs (median return < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for two consecutive months, while consumer demand (GDPC1) remains flat or rising, predicts supply-side stress and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months and GDPC1 >= 0 for the same period
regime_hint: supply shock in a steady demand environment
failure_condition: In 70% of similar supply contractions, the SPX 20-day forward return is non-negative (median p-value > 0.3 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for the first time in three months triggers a one-month positive S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates further policy tightening.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% for the first time in three months
failure_condition: The 1-day SPX forward return is negative in all instances where the trigger occurs (100% failure).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (not directly observable in the provided proxies, but as a counterfactual, a rising RSAFS proxy coupled with a decline in PAYEMS suggests labor market imbalances and a negative 60-day SPX forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases by >2% in a month while PAYEMS decreases by >3% in the same month
failure_condition: In 80% of such labor imbalance triggers, the SPX 60-day forward return is non-negative (median p-value > 0.5).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) growth rate above 0.3% for two consecutive months predicts rising risk premia and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day SPX forward return is non-negative in all instances where the trigger occurs (100% success).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend, separated by at least one month of expansion, precedes a regime shift to supply-side weakness and a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for two months, followed by INDPRO > 102 for one month, then INDPRO < 100 for a second consecutive month
failure_condition: In 80% of such double-dip contractions, the SPX 60-day forward return is non-negative (median p-value > 0.3 in regression).
